The [preceding page](populations-and-samples.qmd) distinguished the finite BOUN release from a broader Turkish usage process. We now introduce an **IID working model** for the accusative indicators and then inspect where that model strains against the corpus design.

## Identical distributions and independence

Let

$$
X_i=
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if personal-pronoun token }i\text{ bears `Case=Acc'},\\
0 & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

The identically distributed claim is

$$
X_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)
$$

for every $i$. It says that each modeled token has the same probability $p$, not that the observed case values are identical.

Conditional mutual independence adds

$$
p(x_1,\ldots,x_n\mid p)
=\prod_{i=1}^n p(x_i\mid p).
$$

Together, the claims are written

$$
X_1,\ldots,X_n\mathrel{\overset{\mathrm{IID}}{\sim}}
\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p).
$$

## An observed sequence

The code loads the audited BOUN extract, estimates the shared probability from all qualifying release rows, and selects the first source-ordered token sequence. Thus neither the outcomes nor the probability are schematic.

```{r}
#| label: load-ud-sequence
library(ggplot2)

pronouns <- read.csv(
  "data/ud-turkish-boun/personal-pronoun-cases.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
p_hat <- mean(pronouns$accusative)
sequence_rows <- pronouns[seq_len(12L),
  c("register", "sentence_id", "form", "case", "accusative")]

sequence_probability <- prod(
  p_hat^sequence_rows$accusative *
    (1 - p_hat)^(1 - sequence_rows$accusative)
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(sequence_rows) == 12L,
  sum(sequence_rows$accusative) == 3L,
  abs(sequence_probability - 0.001081895) < 1e-9
)

sequence_rows
sequence_probability
```

The probability of this exact ordered sequence under the pooled working model is `r format(sequence_probability, digits = 4, scientific = TRUE)`. If the observed sequence contains $k$ accusative tokens, its product has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}
p(\mathbf x\mid p)
&=\prod_{i=1}^{n}p^{x_i}(1-p)^{1-x_i}\\
&=p^k(1-p)^{n-k}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The second line follows because multiplication ignores order after the exact sequence has been observed. A binomial probability for the unordered count would additionally multiply by ${n\choose k}$.

## Inspecting the shared-probability claim

The release preserves five register labels. Their observed accusative proportions expose variation that the pooled model suppresses.

```{r}
#| label: register-proportions
register_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(pronouns, pronouns$register),
  function(x) data.frame(
    register = x$register[1],
    tokens = nrow(x),
    accusative_proportion = mean(x$accusative)
  )
))

ggplot(register_summary,
       aes(register, accusative_proportion, size = tokens)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = p_hat, color = "#8B1A1A", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(color = "grey25") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  labs(x = "BOUN register", y = "Accusative proportion", size = "Tokens") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

Tokens also repeat sentences, and nearby sentences may share documents even though document identifiers are unavailable. The product likelihood is thus a transparent working approximation, not a consequence of the file having distinct rows.

## Check your understanding

1. Which assumption permits the joint probability to factor into token-level probabilities?
2. Why does the ordered-sequence probability omit ${n\choose k}$?
3. Which feature of the plot challenges the identical-distribution assumption?
4. Why can unique token identifiers coexist with dependence?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Conditional mutual independence permits the joint probability to factor into token-level probabilities. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. The calculation concerns one exact ordered sequence. The factor ${n\choose k}$ is needed only when summing over every ordering with the same count. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. The observed accusative proportions differ across BOUN registers, challenging one common token probability. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. Distinct identifiers label rows; they do not prevent rows from sharing a sentence, document, register, or other source of dependence. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>

The [corpus-proportion page](pronoun-case-example.qmd) turns this indicator into an empirical mean and variance.
